 Judgment

This appeal is preferred by the appellant - claimant challenging the judgment & award dated 29th August, 2019 passed in MVC No.1180/2018 by the V Additional Small Causes Judge & Member,
MACT, Court of Small Causes, Mayo Hall Unit, Bengaluru (for short 'the Tribunal).

sentences.text: This appeal is founded on the premise of inadequate and meager compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as under:
NC: 2024:KHC:6657 The claimant was riding a motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA-53-EJ-4195 on 12.12.2017 near Gangapura gate, Kolar-Bangalore NH-75,
Hosakote taluk, at that time a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-03- HP-6142 came in a rash an negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle of the claimant from behind, as a result, the claimant fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
He was immediately shifted to Srinivasa hospital and thereafter to Manipal Hospital, where he was admitted as in-patient for 10 days.

He sustained head injury with right frontoparietal subdur hematoma with bitemporal and right frontal contusion and traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage and other injuries, due to which the claimant spent more than Rs.6,00,000/- towards medical and other incidental expenses.

He was aged 52 years and working as an agriculturist earning Rs.15,000/-
per month.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, the claimant was unable to attend his duty, thereby suffered loss of income.
Hence, he filed the claim petition seeking compensation.

sentences.text: On service of notice, Respondent No.2 did not appear and he was placed exparte.
Respondent No.1 filed the written statement denying the claim of the claimant, but admitted issuance of the policy in favour of respondent No.1.

Respondent No.1 also denied the averments made in the claim petition including age,
avocation, income and negligence attributed against driver of the offending vehicle and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
3.2 Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal framed the relevant issues for consideration.
3.3 In order to substantiate the issues and establish the case, the claimant examined himself as PW.1 and doctor as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P13.
The respondent examined one witness as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R1 and Ex.R2.

3.4 On the basis of the material evidence, both oral and documentary and after hearing learned counsel for the parties, the Tribunal awarded total compensation of NC: 2024:KHC:6657 Rs.3,37,000/- with interest at 9% per annum and directed the respondent No.1/insurer to deposit the compensation amount within two months.
3.5
Being aggrieved by the meager and inadequate compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimant is before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation.

4. It is the vehement contention of learned counsel for the appellant that the income of the appellant assessed by the Tribunal is on the lower side and the compensation awarded under different heads is not in accordance with the material on record.
Therefore, he seeks to allow the appeal and enhance the compensation.
5. Per contra, learned counsel representing the insurance company contends that there is no error, illegality or perversity in the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

He further contends that the Tribunal awarded just and reasonable compensation under all heads, in accordance with the material evidence, NC:
2024:KHC:6657 both oral and documentary and the same does not call for interference.

6. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the material on record, it is seen that the claimant has produced the documents as per Ex.P1 to P13,
out of which, Ex.P1 to Ex.P6 are the Police records, which clearly depict registration of the FIR and laying of charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle and same has not been challenged or controverted.
Therefore, the tribunal rightly attributed the negligence against the rider of the offending vehicle.
Ex. P8
to Ex.P13
are the medical records, which clearly depict the injuries sustained by the claimant in the accident so also the expenses met towards treatment.

7. Though the occurrence of the accident and involvement of the vehicles are not seriously disputed in view of Ex.P1 to Ex.P6, the respondent no.1/insurance company Sri. G.N. Gopal vs The Manager on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67531438/
3 has denied any physical permanent disability or mental cognitive disability due to the occurrence of the NC: 2024:KHC:6657 accident.

The Tribunal having considered the evidence of the doctor and other materials on record concluded that the cognitive disability of the claimant may not affect his avocation i.e., agriculture and declined to grant any compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
However granted compensation on other heads.
8. The tribunal awarded Rs.80,000/- towards pain and suffering.
However, this Court deems it appropriate to award additional amount of Rs.20,000/-.

In all,
Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded under this head.
9. The Tribunal awarded Rs.1,68,768/- towards medical expenses on the basis of the actual bills produced by the claimant, which does not call for interference.
10. The tribunal awarded Rs.10,000/- towards conveyance and Rs.10,000/- towards nourishment and attendant charges, which do not call for interference and the same are retained.
The tribunal awarded Rs.50,000/- towards loss of amenities.
However, this Court deems it appropriate to award additional amount of Rs.25,000/-.
In all, Rs.75,000/- is awarded under this head.
12. The Tribunal awarded Rs.18,000/- towards loss of income during laid up period taking the income of the claimant to be Rs.9,000/-, which is on the lower side.
Considering the magnitude of injuries suffered by the claimant, atleast two months is required to recuperate and get back to normal day to day activities.
Legal Services Authority chart prescribes the notional income of Rs.11,000/- per month for the accident of the year 2017.
Accordingly, the same is taken as income.
Therefore, Rs.22,000/- (Rs.11,000 x 2) is awarded under this head.
13. Learned counsel has made vociferous argument that there being a cognitive disability, it would affect the claimant as he is an agriculturist.
However, nothing cogent evidence is placed before the Court to accept the same.

Moreover, the Tribunal after recording the evidence NC: 2024:KHC:6657 of the claimant has come to the conclusion that there is no difficulty to the claimant to answer the questions posed by the learned counsel for the respondent in the cross- examination and therefore declined to grant any compensation towards loss of future earning capacity on account of disability.

I am in agreement with the learned counsel for the respondent No.1/insurer that there is no proper and substantial material to establish with regard to the mental cognitive disability affecting the work of the claimant.

14. In view of the above, the claimant would be entitled to a total compensation of Rs.3,85,768/- as against Rs.3,36,768/- awarded by the Tribunal, as mentioned in the table below:
